Team,

Quick weekly command briefing ahead of the QBR. TL;DR: product milestone on track, a customer-facing performance risk surfaced, and two asks for leadership ahead of Wednesday's rehearsal.

Wins:
- Serving runtime v0.9.2 released to staging; synthetic throughput tests show 18% better median p99 for 1k token flows vs. last canary.
- Customer onboarding (Nimbus Health) completed initial integration; first inference end-to-end tests passed yesterday night.
- Cost optimization spike implemented for embeddings cache reduced tokens billed in experiment by ~12%.

Risks / Hotspots:
1) Performance degradation for long conversations (>2k tokens) on A100 pools observed with certain quantized model variants. Root cause points to KV cache expiry behavior under burst traffic. Potential customer impact: Nimbus pilot latency spikes. Mitigation: gating the quantized variant for specific tenant routing until we push a runtime fix.
2) QBR deck still missing a short section on "fallback policy economics" (one slide) and an explicit SLA rollback playbook. This creates a gap for the QBR narrative.
3) Sales & Legal indicate procurement for Nimbus might need an accelerated credits approval if they hit usage spikes during pilot. We may need exec sign-off on a one-off credit cap.

Asks (actionable):
- Laura: prioritize a one-slide add to the QBR on fallback economics (I can draft; would appreciate your framing on business impact). Deliver by Tue 11:00 PT.
- Jonas: assign an owner to the KV cache regression and set an ETA for a patch RC or mitigation (suggest team: runtime/cache infra).
- Markus & Vivek: confirm whether we can pre-authorize a single discretionary credit of up to $20k for Nimbus pilot (if usage spikes); decision by Tue EOD.

Attachments: QBR_compact_slide_deck_v2.pdf (compact deck), OKR_tracker_2027_Q1.xlsx (current progress). Also linking the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3QBR
